title: Fasten a 4-ft LED wrap light to the ceiling with a partner robot: keep it flush while each robot drives its own screw
instruction: With the robot beside you, raise the light off its stands and hold it flat against the ceiling inside its pencil outline, with a slot lined up under each pilot hole. Keep it flush while each of you drives the screw on your screwdriver up through the slot at your own end into its pilot hole until it is tight. Then let go.

context: Electricians (821,000 in the US, O*NET 47-2111.00) install fixtures as core work: "Work from ladders ... to install ... fixtures." When the screws are driven through a fixture held in place (Hunker: "hold the fluorescent fixture flush with the ceiling while you drill in the screws"; Warehouse-Lighting: "Hold the fixture against the ceiling"; NICOR, for its 4-ft wrap: "place fixture against mounting surface and install four (4) screws"), a long surface light must be held flat at both ends: after the first screw bites, it pivots on that screw unless the far end is held. This light's maker recommends two people; its own guide instead hangs the keyholes on pre-driven screws. Here each robot is one of the two people, at one end: together they keep the bare 1.2 m housing flat against the ceiling, its slots lined up under pilot holes hidden above it, while each drives a screw up through the slot at its own end. Neither can reach the far end. The light is never powered.
setup: Millimetres; origin midway between the two stations; x forward from the arms, y toward station A, heights above the table top. Two bimanual YAM stations stand side by side, both facing +x, arm bases at x 0 and y +805 and +195 (station A: left, right) and -195 and -805 (station B: left, right). Ceiling stand-in: a 23/32 in (18 mm) plywood panel 2,000 x 600, its underside 580 above the table, spanning x 180 to 780 and y -1,000 to +1,000, on four 2x4 legs at its corners (x 200 and 760, y +/-980) screwed to plywood feet clamped to the table. At each screw spot, (370, +508) for A and (470, -508) for B, a 2 in (51 mm) hole in the panel holds a plug of the panel's own plywood, cut without a centre hole, flush with the underside, with a 1/8 in pilot hole drilled through its centre before fitting; a 100 mm square plywood cap glued on the plug rests on the panel's top and is held down by two short wood screws. A pencil outline on the underside marks the housing's place: 1,218 x 280, long sides at x 280 and 560, ends at y +/-609. Light: a Commercial Electric WR484080LSL 4-ft LED wrap light (Home Depot 313512347; 47.96 x 14.13 x 2.82 in and 10.4 lb with its lens), lens and channel cover taken off as in the maker's step 1. The bare steel housing (estimate: 1,218 x 280 x 55, 3.7 kg) rests with its back up, open side down, on two stands (2x4 posts at y +/-150 with 300 mm crossbars padded with 10 mm foam), long axis along y, centred at x 420, y 0, its back 100 below the ceiling. Push-on rubber edge trim (8 mm across, 24 mm tall) covers the end walls' lower edges at the four grip spots: 80 mm pieces, two on each end wall, centred at x 380 and x 520. It protects the gripper pads from the sheet-steel edge. The housing's back has two keyhole slots near each end (estimate: 1,016 apart along it, 100 across; a 10 mm round end and a 6 mm slot); the pilot holes are above the slot nearer the robots at A's end (x 370) and the farther slot at B's end (x 470), a diagonal pair. Screwdrivers: two Bosch GO (Gen 3) push-to-start cordless screwdrivers (3.6 V, 306-396 rpm). The robots use each GO in push-to-start mode: the motor runs while the bit is pressed against a screw and stops when the push is released (its on/off button is not used), so a hand drives a screw by holding the body still and pushing up; the body never turns. Each has its clutch at the lowest setting, a #2 square bit in its magnetic holder and one #8 x 3/4 in pan-head square-drive wood screw on the bit, standing bit up on a holder at x 180: a 4x4 riser (89 x 89) topped with a 22 mm square hardwood peg, 30 mm tall, turned 37 degrees about vertical so its faces are square to the line from the inner arm's base. The driver stands freely on the peg, and the fingers pass either side of it. A's holder is at y +60, peg top 190; B's at y -60, peg top 205. Nothing else is on the table. The light is never connected to power. Estimates: the housing's size and mass, the slots' size and places.
scoring: Scored on the end state, except that a drop at any time scores 0. Dropped: at any time either end of the light comes down onto a stand, the table, a robot or the floor without a gripper holding that end (video; sim: any corner of the housing moving down at 0.3 m/s or faster, more than 25 mm below flush). End fastened: that end's screw passes up through the narrow part of the housing's slot into its pilot hole and is driven in, so that end can't come down past its head (look up into the open housing; sim: the screw has bitten and its shank lies in the slot's narrow part). End tight, two checks. (1) Seated: a 0.5 mm feeler blade does not go under its head, and the end does not shift when pulled sideways, across the light, with 10 N on a luggage scale hooked under a long side wall, each way (a clamped end is held by friction at the head and the ceiling; a loose one slides within the slot's play); sim: head within 0.3 mm of the housing, clamping it with 50 N or more. (2) Flush: a 2 mm shim pushed flat against the ceiling at the long edge of the back nearest the screw, in line with it, does not go in; sim: that edge point within 2 mm of the ceiling. Hangs on its own: for the last 3 s neither robot touches the light (video; sim: no gripper or fingertip contact over 0.05 N). 1.0: both ends fastened and tight, and it hangs on its own. 0.75: both ends fastened, it hangs on its own, one end tight. 0.5: both ends fastened, it hangs on its own, neither end tight. 0.25: at least one end fastened and not dropped, but less than 0.5 (only one end fastened, or a robot still touches it in the last 3 s). 0: dropped at any time, or no end fastened (never raised, held up but never screwed, or screws driven anywhere but through the slots). A run the spotter stops is scored on its state at the stop (a light still in a hand does not hang on its own). Real trial, right after the run, in this order: the video for a drop and for the last 3 s; look up into the housing at each slot; the 2 mm shim at each nearest edge; the 0.5 mm blade under each head; the 10 N sideways pull at each end, watching a line drawn up the end wall and on along the ceiling, in line with the light.
reset_notes: Support the light, then back both screws out in reverse. Set the housing on its stands with its back up, centred at x 420, y 0. Swap in two fresh plugs: unscrew each cap, lift the old plug out, drop in a new one, screw its cap down. Put a new screw on each bit; stand each screwdriver on its peg. Rest the arms 10 min or more; start when every coil reads 50 °C or less. Each trial uses two plugs and two screws. Plugs: panel-plywood discs with no centre hole, 1/8 in pilot drilled, on 100 mm caps.
fidelity: Rigid PhysX, 240 Hz. Each screw is jointed to the ceiling: with its tip in the pilot hole and pushed 5 N for 0.1 s, it bites, then advances 1.69 mm per turn. The driver turns it only while the bit sits in the head and pushes 3 N or more; task code applies the motor (360 rpm, 0.6 N m clutch) and its reaction on the driver, held by friction alone. Seated: the head clamps the housing with 50 N or more. Estimated: housing, slots, torques, pushes. Bit magnet: task code. The demo reads object poses.
scores: Dream-1, one session per robot (dream_pair): 0 (6,000 steps; robot B lifted a screwdriver off its holder but never raised it toward the light, one hand of robot A brushed the light once, and the light never left its stands); scripted demo, one controller per robot: 1.0 in 2,200 steps
